To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) LRP and MDP1 expression before treatment, and MDR1 expression after treatment are significantly interrelated, (2) LRP expression before any treatment is associated with axillary invasion at the time the mastectomy is performed after induction chemotherapy, and (3) MDR1 expression before or after treatment is associated with the same event.

LRP and MDP1 expression before and after induction chemotherapy, respectively, are independent predictors of axilla node invasion at the rescue mastectomy in patients with locally advanced breast cancer, and that the combination of both markers is the strongest predictor of this outcome.

the expression of MDR1 mRNA and LRP protein in the tumor before treatment, as well as MDR1 mRNA after treatment in the tumor, predicts axillary node metastases at the time of surgery in patients treated with neoadjuvants chemotherapy followed by surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of genes involved in drug resistance in breast cancer.

the study of the expression of genes involved in resistance mechanisms in locally advanced breast tumors before and after treatment, in order to determine their role in the prediction of response to chemotherapy.

the identification of molecular markers that can predict the presence of axillar node invasion in patients with locally advanced breast cancer treated with induction chemotherapy, in order to select those patients who can avoid axillary dissection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of LPR and MDR1 expression before or after chemotherapy, together with the histology and the proliferation index (Ki67) is a powerful predictor of axillary node status in locally advanced breast carcinoma.

the expression of MDR1 mRNA and LRP before treatment and the expression of MDP1 after treatment, are associated with a high probability of axillary node metastatic involvement in patients with locally advanced breast cancer, who are submitted to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by rescue surgery.

, in patients with locally advanced breast cancer who are treated with neoadjuvanet chemotherapy, the expression of LRP and/or MDR1 before or after treatment predicts the presence of axillay node invasion at the rescue mastectomy, and could therefore be useful in the choice of individualized treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of LPR and MDR1 expression before and after neoadjuvant treatment is a good indicator of axillary node status after chemotherapy and rescue surgery.
the expression of the MDR1 and LRP genes in breast cancer is associated with the persistence of chemoresistant tumor clones and, consequently, with a poor prognosis.
the expression of MDR1 and LRP in locally advanced breast tumors, either before or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, predicts axillary node involvement in the rescue mastectomized specimens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in locally advanced breast cancers, the expression of genes involved in resistance, either before or after treatment, is associated with histologically positive axillary lymph nodes after induction chemotherapy.

the expression of MDR1 and LRP in locally advanced breast carcinoma before and/or after neoadjuvant treatment with chemotherapy is a significant predictor of axillary node metastases at the time of surgery, and that this could be helpful in the management of patients with locally advanced breast cancer.
LRP and MDP1 expression before and after chemotherapy is a significant predictor of the presence of metastases in the axillary nodes after chemotherapy and rescue surgery.
